import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

The assurance-contract idea is sound. The packaging in the prompt is not. Do not sell “$10k for one month, then I job-search” inside the first product post.

**Recommended design:** keep the launch post a product post with a short honest closer that links to `/fund`. On that page run two meters: a 30-day one-time threshold for a **named 6-week 1.0 milestone**, and a **recurring** GitHub Sponsors thermometer whose crossing is the only event that pauses interviewing. Implement the threshold as a public pledge ledger that converts to GitHub Sponsors (individuals, 0% on personal sponsorships) and Polar (companies, invoices/VAT) after the goal. Start the job search now. Do not build a Stripe SetupIntent app. Skip Kickstarter unless you can honestly frame a creative 1.0 launch with rewards.

The full analysis is in `research:202610/sase_threshold_pledge_funding__grk.md`.

**Why this shape.** A threshold is the right game theory for a public good (assurance contract / Street Performer Protocol). Card authorization holds last about 7 days, so a 30-day campaign cannot sit on Stripe captures; Kickstarter-class platforms tokenize and charge at the end (~8–10% all-in), which is the mechanism you described and the wrong audience. GitHub Sponsors and Open Collective “goals” are thermometers, not escrow. A one-shot month of salary restores the original problem after 30 days; only recurring money substitutes for a job. The existing launch-post outline already caps ~3,000 words and already has a different §5.2 ask (“out of tokens”).

**Called-out requirement changes:** split tokens vs runway; split one-time milestone vs recurring living costs; gross the goal for fees and tax; land a $2–5k matching pledge first; add a consulting SKU as job-compatible revenue.
